summary: Metadata-only HR, payroll, and accounting app-layer integration envelopes over the flat enterprise domain foundations.

findings: The app crates are thin orchestration surfaces: each function delegates to an already-tested domain evaluator and wraps the result in explicit audit, Workflow, or integration envelope structs.
No generic event bus, async runtime, adapter registry, storage abstraction, or speculative cloud connector was introduced.
Flat microservice package names oya-hr-employment-app, oya-payroll-run-app, and oya-accounting-journal-app preserve independent release and scale ownership.
Envelope contracts carry tenant/legal-entity identity, idempotency keys, evidence refs, and schema versions so future cloud adapters can be added behind explicit runtime evidence gates.

F3_adversarial.failing_fixture_id: domain negative assertions remain in oya-*-domain tests and are exercised transitively by app wrappers
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: App-layer tests assert envelope topics, identifiers, evidence refs, source digests, idempotency, required Workflow steps, and data-class metadata; domain crates still reject invalid refs and incomplete state before app envelopes are produced.
findings: cargo test --locked -p oya-hr-employment-app -p oya-payroll-run-app -p oya-accounting-journal-app passes 7 integration tests.

Public app APIs are named after business actions: onboard_employee, plan_labor_compliance_workflows, close_trial_run, prepare_accounting_dispatch, post_journal_with_audit, plan_vat_workflow, and record_payroll_posting.
Tests are intentionally DAMP and show complete command shapes without needing runtime infrastructure.
Verification passed: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo test for all three app crates; cargo clippy for each app crate with --all-targets and -D warnings.
cargo tree confirms the app crates depend only on their domain crate plus oya-data-boundary-kernel.

alternatives_named: emit audit-chain records directly from app crates
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Metadata-only app envelopes are the smallest integration-ready slice that avoids secrets, network, storage, and false production-readiness claims while giving later runtime adapters typed inputs.
rejected_reasons: REST/cloud adapters require separate API, auth, deployment, SLO, and secrets evidence.
Direct audit-chain emission would couple pure app logic to runtime I/O and exceed this claim.

findings: Every produced envelope carries tenant and/or legal-entity identity from validated domain objects before any future adapter can dispatch it.
No secret material, credentials, HTTP clients, background workers, databases, or file writes were added.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: No prior HR/payroll/accounting app-layer crates existed; no runtime latency or SLO claim is made.

findings.summary: All app functions are synchronous in-memory transformations over bounded domain output vectors; no database, network, async runtime, or polling loop introduced.

findings: All new public app structs carry data_class comments, and tests assert critical runtime Classified wrappers for PII/FINANCIAL/PUBLIC/INTERNAL_ONLY metadata.
The app layer does not encode tax rates, statutory filing transport, ledger persistence, payment execution, or payroll compliance certification.

Additive workspace members and catalog rows can be reverted by removing the three app crate directories, their registry/per-service catalog rows, spec AC-06/decision-log additions, and Cargo.toml members. No migration or persisted data exists.

App functions return audit/Workflow/integration envelope values with topics and schema versions, but do not emit telemetry or audit-chain records at runtime. Runtime emitters remain a later adapter slice.
The slice extends the already-landed flat domain foundations; no external API, database schema, or wire contract exists yet, so compatibility risk is limited to workspace consumers.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: Building app-layer crates before cloud integration is useful only if they remain pure metadata envelope builders and avoid runtime I/O.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: tasks/enterprise-microservices-plan.md#CS-ENT-APP-001 + cargo tree output for each app crate
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Later cloud adapters would have to invent audit/workflow/accounting envelope shapes while also handling runtime concerns, increasing coupling and false-readiness risk.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Waiting for full cloud/runtime integration would delay type-safe envelope contracts; app crates are additive and reversible.

findings: Fits ADR-0315 compositional ERP doctrine by keeping HR, Payroll, and Accounting as separate services joined through typed evidence refs, source digests, and idempotent metadata envelopes.
Package names follow oya-<microservice>-<bounded-context>-app: oya-hr-employment-app, oya-payroll-run-app, and oya-accounting-journal-app.
tasks/enterprise-microservices-plan.md and tasks/enterprise-microservices-todo.md document the app slice and honest non-claims.
Implementation resides under microservices/hr|payroll|accounting/crates/*-app with matching per-service and central catalog rows.
No storage, network, Workflow execution, audit-chain runtime emission, regulator filing, payment execution, or cloud adapter introduced.
Each app package depends only on oya-data-boundary-kernel plus its same-service domain package.
HR, Payroll, and Accounting specs gained AC-06 app-envelope acceptance refs pointing to existing app integration tests.
App algorithms are deterministic wrappers over domain outputs and preserve domain-generated idempotency/evidence metadata where available.
